title: Day 769: Week-Long Sweep Across All 20 Sinaloa Municipalities Yields 16 Detained, 40 Explosive Devices Seized
detail: The Sinaloa Secretaría de Seguridad Pública (SSP) reported Monday, August 31, 2026 that coordinated deployments across all 20 of the state's municipalities during the week of August 23–30 — run by municipal police, the State Preventive Police, the Armed Forces, SEDENA, the federal Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana, the National Guard and the Secretaría de Marina — resulted in 16 detentions. Seizures included 22 firearms, 115 magazines, 3,048 cartridges, one hand grenade, 40 improvised explosive devices, seven vehicles, one armored vehicle, 248 grams of suspected crystal methamphetamine, and 11 tactical vests. Officials said the sustained operations, launched amid the ongoing Chapitos–Mayos faction dispute that has driven violence in Sinaloa since September 2024, were intended to "inhibir hechos delictivos" statewide. The tally rolls up several individual operations reported during the week, including an August 29 action credited with eight detentions, weapons, explosives and drugs.

media.caption: Weapons, explosives and vehicles seized during a week-long security sweep across Sinaloa's 20 municipalities, reported August 31, 2026

title: Day 769: Army and Police Blanket Schools Statewide as Sinaloa Starts 2026–2027 School Year
detail: Mexican Army personnel, alongside state and municipal police, deployed a security operation covering schools in all 20 of Sinaloa's municipalities on Monday, August 31, 2026, the first day of the 2026–2027 school year, following the funeral-wreath threat left overnight at a Culiacán private school. A permanent surveillance point was established at the threatened campus, and companion Infobae reporting described children statewide now regularly practicing lockdown and shooting-response drills as part of routine school safety preparation amid the ongoing cartel conflict. Officials framed the operation as part of broader efforts, alongside interim Governor Graciela Domínguez Nava's federal-backed security and governance plan, to reassure families as classes resumed.

media.caption: Soldiers stand guard at a Sinaloa school as the 2026-2027 academic year begins under heightened security, August 31, 2026
